829. Since Religion resides in the highest parts of a person, and from those highest parts the lower elements live and shine, and because **Mohammed** <note>original: "Mahumedes"</note> is present in their minds along with their religion, some Mohammed is always placed in their sight. So that they may turn their faces toward the East, over which the Lord is, he is placed below the Christian **Center** <note>original: "Meditullium"</note>. This is not the actual Mohammed who wrote the **Koran** <note>original: "Alcoranum"</note>, but another who performs his office; nor is it always the same person, but he is changed. Once there was one from **Saxony** who, having been captured by the **Algerians** <note>original: "Algiriensibus"</note>, became a Mohammedan. Because he had also been a Christian, he was occasionally moved to speak with them about the Lord, saying that He was not the Son of Joseph, but the Son of God Himself. Other Mohammeds succeeded this one later. In the place where that representative Mohammed has his seat, a fire appears like torches so that he may be known; but that fire is not visible to any others except the Mohammedans.

830. The actual Mohammed who wrote the Koran does not come into view today. I was told that in the earliest times he presided over them, but because he wished to rule over all things of their Religion as a God, he was ejected from his seat—which he held beneath the Roman Catholics—and sent down to the right side near the south. Once, when a certain society of Mohammedans was stirred up by malicious spirits to acknowledge Mohammed as God, in order to settle the sedition, Mohammed was raised up from the lower earth and shown to them; and I also saw him then. He appeared similar to corporeal spirits who have no interior perception, his face bordering on black, and I heard him speaking these words: *I am your Mohammed*; and soon after he seemed to sink down.

831. The Mohammedans are hostile to Christians primarily because of the faith in three Divine Persons, and the resulting worship of three Gods, and just as many Creators; and toward the **Roman Catholics** <note>original: "Chatolico-Romanis"</note> additionally because of their kneeling before images. Consequently, they call the latter **Idolaters** <note>original: "Idololatras"</note> and the former fanatics, saying that they make a three-headed God, and that they say "One" but mutter "Three," thereby splitting Omnipotence and making three out of the one and only. They say Christians are like **Fauns** with three horns, one for each God, and yet three for one; and that they thus pray, thus sing, and thus sound from their pulpits.

832. Like all nations that acknowledge one God, love what is just, and do good from a religious motive, the Mohammedans have their own Heaven, but it is outside the Christian one. Yet the Mohammedan Heaven is divided into two: in the lower one, they live honorably with several wives, but no others are raised from there into the higher Heaven except those who give up their concubines and acknowledge the Lord our Savior, and at the same time His dominion over Heaven and Hell. I heard that it is impossible for them to think of God the Father and our Lord as being one, but it is possible for them to believe that He rules over the Heavens and Hells because He is the Son of God the Father. This is the faith among them through which the Lord grants them ascent into the higher Heaven.

833. That the Mohammedan religion is accepted by more kingdoms than the Christian religion may be a stumbling block to those who think about **Divine Providence** and at the same time believe that no one can be saved except one born a Christian. But the Mohammedan religion is no stumbling block to those who believe that all things are of Divine Providence; these people inquire into its purpose and they find it. It is this: that the Mohammedan religion acknowledges the Lord as the Greatest Prophet, the Wisest of all, and also as the Son of God; but because they have made the Koran alone the book of their religion, and thus Mohammed, who wrote it, has settled in their thoughts and they follow him with some worship, they think little about our Lord. In order that it may be fully known that this religion was raised up by the Lord's Divine Providence to destroy the idolatries of many nations, it will be described in some order; but first, concerning the origin of idolatries. Before that religion, there was **idolatrous** worship...

<summary>Swedenborg describes the state of Muslims in the spiritual world, noting their representative leaders and their criticisms of the Christian Trinity. He explains that their religion serves a providential purpose in combating older forms of idolatry.</summary>
